item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It was indeed violent, but i think each iteration of the tests were useful in a way since they all revealed a different aspect of SCP-841's functions and the full extend of its limitations.

First test revealed it was indeed a mirror voodoo doll, as stated by the auction house but not much more.

Second test showed the doll wasn't limited in its movement range, even though it mimicked the human's movement in the first place, and that the doll's movement could supercede the human's ones, as implied by the pressure felt by the D subject.

Third test revealed an "infinite movement loop" was possible, to the point of dismemberment.

The fourth one showed that SCP-841's effects were persistent after physical contact was broken with the doll since no one tried throwing it before, it also showed only the limbs "movement" is retained and, and visibly no impact or other forms of damages transfer to the human body.

The last test remains unclear though, it clearly show the twine isn't as important as the wooden limbs, but can't really explain if the decapitation was due the twine being imbued by SCP-841's anomalous properties or by the wooden head being taken appart from the rest of the doll.

The first case would show the head being cut, or at least ripped in a clean way while the second case would show a crude decapitation due to the subject's head being ripped off.

Still we do learn that the twine can be replaced. But the logical next course of action would have been to test the beheaded doll with a last subject.

And eventually to try and take a wood sample for analysis.

This SCP feels great and the claims of unneeded violence could be mitigated if a short conclusion was added after each test so they wouldn't seem so gratuitous.

item.title: Notes on a rewrite
item.content:encoded:
Notes Here!
Accursed Note! I Spit At Thee!!!!

First: it's interesting that the anomalous effect persists even when the twine is entirely replaced. Might be best to keep the parts separate, I think.

Second: this SCP will live or die not on its anomalous properties — because I don't think there's that much that can be changed in that respect — but on its interactions and backstory. I think the key point to consider here is that this is a made thing. Someone made this. "The twine has uneven signs of wear on different joints, suggesting that the figure has been damaged and repaired at least once" - someone cared enough about it to fix it; how could they have done so without being horribly killed? And how would the item have come to the attention of the Foundation?

What I'm thinking… is in terms of what's called "naive art", "outsider art" (and no, this is not an AWCY artifact, stop complaining). It's very crude… one might say it doesn't show much sign of skill on the part of the maker.

I'm thinking about MC&D. I'm thinking about where they get their items — some they steal, some they loot, some they buy.

Some bumbling amateur made this thing as a Fun Craft Project, and thought it was so great that it was obviously worth huge amounts of money. And one aspect of MC&D that few writers take into account is that they're a business. They rely on customers… so they can't treat their customers too rudely, even if the customers are idiots. Consider what kind of idiocy you would get from customers who revel in being super-decadent and super-rich… and who have access to anomalies.

All dealers in antiquities (and collectibles, and art, and used books, and…) have their stories about the idiots who come in with near-worthless crap that they insist is super valuable. Now imagine that the idiot is a repeat customer who's responsible for >1% of your organization's annual gross income.

"Look what I made!"

"It's lovely, sir. You are truly gifted. May I ask what it is?"

"I made it using the [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] that I bought from you last year, and the [REDACTED] that you sold to my friend [REDACTED] before his [DATA EXPUNGED]! And I whittled the wood myself using a knife that [DATA EXPUNGED], and the trees grew in [DATA EXPUNGED], and -"

"Fascinating, sir. But… what is it?"

"It's a reverse mirror voodoo puppet!"

"I'm sorry, sir, a what?"

"Reverse mirror voodoo stick puppet!"

"A mirror voodoo—"

"REVERSE mirror!"

"But, sir, a mirror already… yes sir. A reverse mirror voodoo stick puppet. Very impressive. You are a true artist."

"Yeah! So what'll you give me for it?"

"…. I beg your pardon?"

"I'm selling it to you! What'll you give me for it!"

"I, uh, sir, I… I'm not authorized to make purchases on behalf of my employer, sir. I'll need to speak to my supervisor."

"Sure, you do that. This little baby oughta go for eight, maybe nine million?"

"Uh. Sir, I… please realize that the prices for which we sell items are not the prices we pay for items, and… "

"Yeah, yeah, I gotcha. So… eighty, ninety grand?"

"Sir, really, I'm not authorized to make purchases on behalf of… sir, what does the reverse mirror voodoo stick puppet even do?"

"Pick it up."

"Uh…."

"No, take it out of the towel. Let it touch your skin!"

"Sir, I am a client interaction representative, not a test subject. If you wish to purchase a human test subject for demonstration purposes, that can be arranged as a separate transaction."

Edit: Sorry, bud, but that was awful big. -TroyL

item.title: Re: Destruction
item.content:encoded:
Using up D-class personnel like kleenex while testing or containing a Keter-class SCP = okay (remember, some containment protocols include a 'terminate everyone directly involved' contingency).

Using up D-class personnel like kleenex while testing a Euclid-class SCP = well, okay. If it's necessary.

Using up D-class personnel like kleenex while testing a Safe-class SCP = please try to be more careful.

Using up D-class personnel like kleenex so that Dr. Randall can jerk off while testing a Safe-class SCP = we're going to have to do something about Dr. Randall's misuse of Foundation resources. If he's willing to do this with one SCP, he might do it with others.

Either Dr. Randall needs to be reprimanded, disciplined and/or reassigned, or this thing induces horrific levels of sexual sadism and needs to be reclassified as Euclid.

"And if you take a look at the log there are some plainly needless fatalities in there."

Yes. This is the point. For goodness sake, look at the last one! Randall ripped off somebody's head and played with her corpse for half an hour! Read between the lines of the test log, this is a sadist using Foundation resources to torture and kill Class-D's — and predominantly female Class-D's, if you pay attention to the pronouns.

This SCP isn't about a birchwood doll. This SCP is about how easy it is for somebody like Randall to thrive within the Foundation.

Also, hint: There was no inbuilt safety function in the gauntlets.
